courseTitle: How IT Teams Work: Agile, Waterfall, Scrum, Kanban & Software Releases

slots.practicalActivity: Write a comparison chart contrasting Waterfall's phases (Requirements, Design, Build, Test, Release, Maintenance) against a 2-week Scrum sprint cycle (Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review, Retrospective); then write 3 original user stories in the 'As a [role], I want [capability], so that [benefit]' format for a retail sales dashboard request, each with at least 2 checkable acceptance criteria.
slots.deliverable: A written Waterfall-vs-Scrum comparison chart, plus 3 original user stories with acceptance criteria.

slots.practicalActivity: Sketch a 5-column Kanban board (Backlog, To Do, In Progress, Review, Done) with at least 6 realistic cards, including one tagged Blocked and one tagged Off Track, and set a WIP limit for the In Progress column with a one-sentence justification for why it helps the team finish work rather than just start it; then map a single change through the Dev -> QA -> UAT -> Production chain, writing one sentence per stage naming who owns it and what question that stage answers.
slots.deliverable: A sketched Kanban board with a WIP limit and status-tagged cards, plus a written Dev/QA/UAT/Production walkthrough for one change.

slots.practicalActivity: In a scratch folder, run git init, create a feature branch with git checkout -b, make a small change to a text file, stage it, and commit it with a descriptive message (not 'fixed stuff'); if you have GitHub access, push the branch and open a pull request. Then diagram a CI/CD pipeline for that same change (Code Commit -> Automated Tests -> Build -> Deploy to Staging -> Deploy to Production) and write a short release checklist covering approval, monitoring, a rollback plan, and release notes.
slots.deliverable: A real local Git repository with at least one feature branch and one descriptive commit, plus a written CI/CD pipeline diagram and release checklist.

slots.practicalActivity: Using the Castlebridge Retail scenario from this course ('Our regional managers keep asking me for last month's numbers by email. I need a dashboard that shows revenue by region and by product category, updated automatically...'), write the full chain from request to release in miniature: 2-3 user stories with acceptance criteria, a Kanban board layout showing where each story sits, which environment (Dev/QA/UAT/Production) each story is currently in, and one deployment risk-reduction strategy (blue-green, canary, rolling, or feature flag) you'd use for the launch and why.
slots.deliverable: A one-page written plan tracing a single business request through user stories, a Kanban board, the Dev/QA/UAT/Production chain, and a chosen deployment strategy.

slots.practicalActivity: Complete the Real-World IT Project Simulation capstone end to end for Castlebridge Retail: write user stories (with acceptance criteria) for the revenue-by-region view, the revenue-by-category view, and the automatic daily refresh; build a 5-column Kanban board and place the stories on it; write a QA test plan that includes the zero-sales-region edge case; write a one-paragraph UAT sign-off in the sales director's own voice; write concrete, specific release notes (not 'various improvements'); and write up how you'd investigate and what you'd communicate during a simulated production incident where a region's revenue shows zero two days after launch.
slots.deliverable: A complete written capstone package: user stories with acceptance criteria, a Kanban board, a QA test plan, a UAT sign-off, release notes, and a production-incident response writeup.

monthlyMilestoneContribution: After finishing this course, a student can speak the shared vocabulary of a real IT department -- Agile/Scrum ceremonies, Kanban boards, the Dev/QA/UAT/Production release chain, Git version control, and CI/CD deployment strategies -- and apply all of it to a single real business request end to end.
